en: Today we are going to look at opportunity cost and why it matters for every decision.
Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative that you give up.
If you spend two hours studying, the opportunity cost might be two hours of paid work.
Scarcity means that we cannot have everything we want at the same time.
Supply and demand together determine the market price of a good.
When demand increases and supply stays the same, the equilibrium price goes up.
A price ceiling set below equilibrium will usually create a shortage.
A price floor above equilibrium tends to create a surplus.
Elasticity measures how strongly quantity responds to a change in price.
Demand for basic food is usually inelastic in the short run.
Luxury goods often have a high income elasticity of demand.
Marginal cost is the extra cost of producing one more unit.
Firms maximize profit where marginal revenue equals marginal cost.
In perfect competition, no single firm can influence the market price.
A monopoly can restrict output in order to raise the price.
Market failure happens when the market does not allocate resources efficiently.
Pollution is a classic example of a negative externality.
Education creates a positive externality because society also benefits.
The government may use a tax to correct a negative externality.
Public goods are non-rival and non-excludable.
Comparative advantage explains why countries gain from trade.
Even if one country is better at everything, both can still benefit from specialization.
Gross domestic product measures the total value of final goods and services.
Nominal GDP is not adjusted for inflation, but real GDP is.
Inflation is a general increase in the price level over time.
Last year inflation did not exceed three percent.
High inflation reduces the purchasing power of money.
Unemployment rose to six point two percent during the recession.
A recession is often defined as two consecutive quarters of negative growth.
Monetary policy is controlled by the central bank.
When the central bank raises the interest rate, borrowing becomes more expensive.
Lower interest rates can encourage investment and consumption.
Fiscal policy refers to government spending and taxation.
Expansionary fiscal policy can increase aggregate demand.
The exchange rate is the price of one currency in terms of another.
A weaker currency makes exports cheaper for foreign buyers.
The law of diminishing marginal utility says each extra unit gives less satisfaction.
Consumers try to maximize utility given their budget constraint.
The production possibility frontier shows the trade-offs an economy faces.
Points inside the frontier mean resources are not fully used.
Economic growth shifts the production possibility frontier outward.
Fixed costs do not change with the level of output.
Variable costs rise as the firm produces more.
In the long run, all costs are variable.
Economies of scale lower the average cost as output grows.
Barriers to entry protect firms with market power.
Price discrimination means charging different prices to different customers.
An oligopoly is a market with only a few large firms.
Game theory helps us understand strategic behavior between firms.
The prisoner's dilemma shows why cooperation can be hard to maintain.
Sunk costs should not affect rational decisions about the future.
People do not always behave rationally, as behavioral economics shows.
A budget deficit occurs when spending is greater than revenue.
Government debt is the accumulation of past deficits.
The multiplier effect means an initial change in spending has a larger final impact.
Savings and investment are linked through the financial system.
A bond is a promise to repay a loan with interest.
Stock prices reflect expectations about future profits.
Diversification reduces risk but never removes it completely.
That is all for today; please read chapter four before Thursday.
Now let's switch to the computer science part of the course.
An algorithm is a finite sequence of well-defined steps.
Big O notation describes how running time grows with input size.
Binary search runs in logarithmic time on a sorted array.
A hash table offers average constant-time lookups.
Recursion is when a function calls itself on a smaller problem.
Every recursive function needs a base case, otherwise it never stops.
A stack follows last in, first out order.
A queue follows first in, first out order.
Dynamic programming stores the answers to overlapping subproblems.
A graph consists of vertices connected by edges.
Dijkstra's algorithm finds shortest paths when edge weights are not negative.
Machine learning models learn patterns from data rather than explicit rules.
Overfitting means the model memorizes the training data and fails on new data.
We split the data into training, validation and test sets.
A neural network is made of layers of simple computing units.
The learning rate controls how large each gradient step is.
Precision and recall are not the same metric.
An API defines how two software components talk to each other.
Latency is the time between a request and its response.
Throughput is how many requests a system can handle per second.
A database index speeds up reads but can slow down writes.
Transactions should be atomic, consistent, isolated and durable.
Never store passwords in plain text; store a salted hash instead.
Encryption protects data both in transit and at rest.
Version control lets a team track every change to the code.
Unit tests check small pieces of code in isolation.
Concurrency bugs often appear only under heavy load.
A deadlock happens when two threads wait for each other forever.
The operating system schedules processes on the available CPU cores.
Virtual memory gives each process the illusion of a large private address space.
Cache misses can make a fast algorithm slow in practice.
Open source software can be inspected and modified by anyone.
Cloud computing lets you rent servers instead of buying them.
Containers package an application together with its dependencies.
Hardly any real system is perfectly secure.
About ninety percent of the effort goes into the last ten percent of the features.
None of these techniques work without clean data.
